items.excerpt: AI hasn’t just dominated the tech world through the first half of this year — its use and applications have dominated the buzz in nearly every aspect of our lives from employment to dating. That has been true in the venture capital and investing world as well.
items.title: ‘Excited’ And ‘Scary’: After Sizzling First Half, Don’t Expect AI Investment To Cool Off

items.excerpt: Recent coverage of private market data has surprised many by revealing the extent to which European venture capital has outperformed American venture capital in recent history. Equidam’s Dan Gray explains how that happened.
items.title: Why European VC Is Outperforming The US

items.excerpt: Despite the seemingly happy conclusion of last week’s OpenAI drama, is all really back to normal in the ecosystem? Yael Benjamin, founder of data-sharing platform Startup Snapshot shares what a poll of global tech stakeholders found.
items.title: What Are The Long-Term Implications Of The OpenAI Chaos On The Tech Ecosystem?

items.excerpt: Food shoppers today are quite familiar with traditional foods made from nontraditional ingredients, and judging from the ranks of funded food startups, the trend is far from over. We take a look at where the money’s going.
items.title: Startups Still See A Future In Familiar Foods Made With Weird Ingredients

items.excerpt: We spoke to Ryan Hinkle, managing director at startup investor Insight Partners, about where he sees long-awaited liquidity exits coming into play in 2024.
items.title: Insight Partners’ Hinkle: M&A Is The Key To Unlocking Startup Liquidity This Year

items.excerpt: The startup industry has settled into a new, healthy normal where valuations have returned to reasonable levels, but will that lead us to a Goldilocks scenario? Guest author Marc Schröder of MGV shares what that is and what it will take to achieve it.
items.title: The Goldilocks Scenario Every VC Is Hoping For

items.excerpt: The bar for Series A investment appears much higher in 2024 and fewer startups are reaching it, writes guest author Dan Gray of Equidam. He explains the valuation conundrum many of today’s venture investors face and what we can expect to see in the future.
items.title: Crossing The Series A Chasm

items.excerpt: We take a look at some of the biggest issues VCs and founders likely are watching as the presidential election looms only days away.
items.title: The US Presidential Election Will Affect Venture Investing. How Much Is The Question

items.excerpt: 2024 has been a year of rapid progress and high expectations for the fintech sector, explains Katherine Maslova of Bourgeois Bohème, but certain trends are more aspirational than practical. In this guest column, Maslova breaks down what she means by that.
items.title: For Fintech, 2024 Was A Year of Hype, Hustle and Hard Truths. What’s Next In 2025?

items.excerpt: While global venture investment rebounded last year, the Asia funding market cratered, totaling only $65.8 billion in 2024 — the exact same low the market hit in 2014.
items.title: Asia Venture Funding Tanks To 10-Year Low

items.excerpt: The startup world begins 2025 on a decidedly more upbeat note than it did the previous year. The renewed optimism is in part due to the modest uptick in venture funding last year, when global startup investment finally topped pre-pandemic levels again.
items.title: Forecast Digest: IPO, M&A And Venture Markets Expected To Gain In 2025

items.excerpt: While bubbles, deception, spin and outright misrepresentation seem to have become the norm in today’s startup and VC market, there are solutions. In this guest commentary, Mikhail Taver, founder and managing partner of Taver Capital Partners, shares some of his thoughts.
items.title: The House of Cards Built By Startups And VCs: Can Trust Be Restored?

items.title: Breaking The Wealth Barrier: Why The SEC Should Redefine ‘Accredited Investor’

items.excerpt: There’s a pretty fat pipeline of venture-backed fintech startups that meet the basic criteria for an IPO. The list of likeliest suspects, however, includes many familiar names that have so far resisted the call of the public markets.

items.excerpt: While the IPO market remains unpredictable, global dealmaking across M&A and private capital investment is showing strong momentum. In this guest commentary, Nithya B. Das of Diligent Corp. shares key pillars of capital and transaction readiness for companies, regardless of whether they’re planning
items.title: Beyond The IPO: Why Capital And Transaction Readiness Is A Business Imperative

items.excerpt: After several quiet years, it appears that 2025 may be the year that the U.S. market finally sees a flurry of fintech IPOs. Here are some of the companies we’re keeping our eyes on.
items.title: Here Are The Fintech Companies That Could Go Public In 2025

items.excerpt: A total of $12.6 billion was raised by around 1,200 startups across Europe last quarter, with funding amounts comparable with the previous two quarters. And for the first time since 2012, Germany-based startups jumped ahead of the United Kingdom by amounts invested in a quarter.
items.title: Germany Leapfrogs UK To Lead European VC Investment In Q2 As Region’s Funding Settles

items.excerpt: The venture market recovery isn’t a recovery at all, according to guest author Steve Brotman, who writes that what we’re seeing today is consolidation. items.title: Why Venture’s Future Is Being Decided By A Select Few

items.excerpt: This year is on track to outpace last year for the number of startups buying their venture-backed peers, Crunchbase data shows. We speak with M&A advisers about the factors underlying those trends, and what to expect for the remainder of 2025.
items.title: Why More Startups Are Buying Other Startups In 2025

items.excerpt: Hollywood’s integration of AI tools is reshaping the very nature of storytelling, the economic lifelines of creative workers, and the power dynamics that govern the industry, writes Aron Solomon. In this guest commentary he lays out the best path forward as the industry faces the crossroads.
items.title: AI In Hollywood: Reinventing Creativity Or Redrawing The Lines Of Power?

items.excerpt: Prolific hacking group Scattered Spider is able to successfully use compromised employee credentials in their attacks. Jason Martin, co-founder and co-CEO of Permiso Security, shares how businesses can work to protect themselves.
items.title: The Billion-Dollar Security Threat: All Industries On Guard

items.title: Startups And The Shutdown: When Your Primary Customer Folds Overnight
